summary: Phoenix contains numerous silent suppression handlers and broad exception handlers that obscure failure modes without explicit degraded status. While fallbacks are present, many lack clear evidence-gate blocking (MISSING/BLOCKED) and could inadvertently affect decision-making. The proposal correctly identifies targets but requires stricter validation of fallback contracts before removal.
top_technical_reasons: 32 bare-pass candidates (e.g., src/agents.py:126, src/precompute.py:52) return success without explicit degraded status, violating evidence-gate requirements.
Broad exception handlers (e.g., in src/data_module.py, src/nvidia_ai.py) may suppress failures silently, risking undetected degradation.
Fixed fallbacks (e.g., src/phoenix/pricing.py, src/basket/autocall.py) lack contract tests to ensure they do not affect selection criteria.
Duplicate provider/network calls remain unmeasured, risking redundant computation without clear freshness semantics.

candidate_safety.fallback_visibility: explicit but requires stricter evidence-gate enforcement

next_experiments.hypothesis: Replacing bare-pass handlers with explicit MISSING/BLOCKED status will not break intentional fallbacks or degrade performance.
next_experiments.change: Replace silent success returns in bare-pass candidates (e.g., src/agents.py:126) with MISSING/BLOCKED status where caller cannot distinguish failure.
next_experiments.metric_gate: Full test suite passes, no regression in frozen key outputs, and no evidence-gate weakening.
next_experiments.why_it_is_informative: Validates that explicit failure handling does not introduce new risks while improving transparency.

next_experiments.hypothesis: Auditing fallback_defaults and fixed model fallbacks will reveal contracts that should block evidence rather than return fabricated values.
next_experiments.change: Audit fallback_defaults (src/data_module.py) and fixed fallbacks (src/phoenix/pricing.py) to ensure they return MISSING/BLOCKED when evidence is insufficient.
next_experiments.metric_gate: No regression in fallback behavior, and all acceptance gates pass.
next_experiments.why_it_is_informative: Ensures fallbacks do not inadvertently pass evidence gates, aligning with safety constraints.

next_experiments.hypothesis: Measuring and caching duplicate provider/network calls will reduce redundant computation without affecting freshness semantics.
next_experiments.change: Instrument and measure duplicate calls in src/external_data.py and src/agents.py, then cache results where freshness is preserved.
next_experiments.metric_gate: Reduction in call count with no degradation in data freshness or model performance.
next_experiments.why_it_is_informative: Quantifies inefficiency and validates that caching does not compromise evidence integrity.

data_or_label_risks.silent_suppression: High risk: Bare-pass handlers may hide failures, leading to undetected degradation in model performance.
data_or_label_risks.fallback_contracts: Medium risk: Fixed fallbacks may return values that affect selection criteria without explicit blocking.
data_or_label_risks.duplicate_work: Low risk: Redundant calls increase latency but do not fabricate data.
data_or_label_risks.evidence_gate_weakening: Medium risk: Some fallbacks may inadvertently pass evidence gates without proper MISSING/BLOCKED status.
